title: You Are Not Behind. God Doesn't Use a Timeline You Can See.
fullText: You are comparing your chapter 3 to someone else's chapter 20. And the comparison is making you believe something that is not true. It's making you believe you are behind, behind where you're supposed to be, behind your peers, behind some invisible schedule that everyone around you seems to be keeping except you. Behind the version of your life you thought you'd have by now. And here is what that belief does. It turns every season of your life into evidence of failure. The waiting becomes proof you did something wrong. The delay becomes confirmation that God has forgotten you. The season you're in, whatever it is, becomes something to escape rather than something to inhabit. But I want to show you something in the Bible that will permanently change how you measure time. In scripture, God does not operate on a visible timeline. He does not measure progress the way you measure it. He does not define on time the way you define it. And every person he ever used significantly was by every human measure of timing. Late, wrong age, wrong season, wrong moment and exactly where God needed them to be. If you have been measuring your life against a clock that God never gave you, this is for you. Before we go through the examples, I need to name the thing that's actually happening beneath the surface of the comparison. When you feel behind, you are not just experiencing impatience. You are making a theological claim. You are saying implicitly, I know what God's timeline for my life is supposed to look like, and this is not it. That is a significant assumption because nowhere in scripture does God hand anyone a schedule. Nowhere does he say by age 30 you should have this, by age 35 you should have accomplished that. The timeline you are measuring yourself against was assembled from somewhere else from culture from comparison from what worked for someone whose assignment is entirely different from yours. Ecclesiastes 3:11 says, "God has made everything beautiful in its time." And then it says something that rarely gets quoted alongside that verse. He has also set eternity in the human heart. Yet no one can fathom what God has done from beginning to end. Read that carefully. God set eternity the full ark of his purposes in your heart. But he made it so you cannot see it completely. You have the sense that there is something significant ahead. But you cannot see the full timeline from where you stand. And that is not a design flaw. It is intentional. Because if you could see the full timeline, you would not need to trust the one who holds it. The feeling of being behind is almost always a symptom of trying to see more of the timeline than God has given you access to. The clearest example in all of scripture is Abraham. And I want to go through it slowly because the details matter. Abraham was 75 years old when God first made the promise. 75. He had no children. Sarah was barren. And God told him that he would become the father of many nations, that his descendants would be as numerous as the stars in the sky and the sand on the seashore. By any human timeline, the moment for this promise had already passed. A 75-year-old man with a barren wife is not a promising starting point for a great nation. Any reasonable observer would have said, "You are too late. The window has closed. This is not going to happen." But God was not working on a human timeline. Abraham was 85 when God reaffirmed the covenant. Still no child. He was 99 years old when God appeared to him again, changed his name from Abraham to Abraham, father of many nations, and told him that within a year Sarah would give birth. Sarah was 90. She laughed when she heard it. Genesis 18:12 records what she thought inside the tent. After I am worn out and my lord is old, will I now have this pleasure? She was not being cynical. She was being realistic. The math did not work. The biology did not work. Nothing about the timing worked. And Isaac was born the following year. Abraham was 100 years old. 25 years between the promise and the fulfillment. 25 years of watching other people's families grow while his remained empty. 25 years of the gap between what God had said and what Abraham could see. And notice God did not apologize for the timeline. He did not explain the delay. He simply asked when he heard Sarah's laughter. Is anything too hard for the Lord? Here is what that 25-year weight produced that a 5-year weight could not have. By the time Isaac was born, it was biologically impossible for Abraham and Sarah to have produced him on their own. There was no human explanation for the child. The only explanation was God. And that was the point. The delay was not a malfunction in the timeline. The delay was the mechanism by which the miracle would be unambiguous. If the child had been born earlier, human biology could have taken the credit. At 190, there was no other explanation. The thing you are waiting for may be timed precisely so that when it arrives there is only one possible explanation for it. Let me ask you a question before we continue and I want you to sit with it honestly. When you say you feel behind behind what exactly? Behind whom? Where did that timeline come from? Who handed it to you and told you it was God's? Because here is what often happens. Someone around you gets married, gets promoted, launches something significant, has a child, and without realizing it, their timeline becomes the template for yours. Their chapter 20 becomes your chapter 3, and you spend your energy grieving a schedule that was never yours to begin with. The comparison is not just emotionally damaging, it is theologically confused. It assumes that God is running the same story for every person at the same pace. And the Bible does not support that assumption, not once. The second example I want to take you to is one of the most quietly devastating stories in the Gospels. And it is about a man whose experience of divine timing was nothing like what he expected. John the Baptist had dedicated his entire life to one purpose, preparing the way for the Messiah. Everything he did, the wilderness, the locusts and wild honey, the camelhair clothing, the relentless preaching, all of it was directed toward one end. He knew what he was called to do. He did it faithfully. He baptized Jesus in the Jordan River. He heard the voice from heaven. He said, "Behold the lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world." And then he was arrested and put in prison. And he [clears throat] sat there while Jesus, the one he had announced, the one his entire life had been building toward, was out doing miracles, healing the sick, preaching the kingdom, doing the very things John had said he would do. And from inside his prison cell, John sent two of his disciples to ask Jesus a question. Luke 7:19. The question was this. Are you the one who is to come, or shall we look for another? This is not a casual theological inquiry. This is a man in a dungeon facing execution who had given everything to a calling he was now watching from a distance and wondering whether he had understood it correctly. It is one of the most human moments in all of the gospels. And Jesus's response to that question is worth examining carefully. He did not answer it directly. He told John's disciples, "Go and tell John what you hear and see the blind receive their sight, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the poor have good news preached to them." And then he added one sentence that has always struck me as one of the most tender things Jesus ever said. "Blessed is the one who is not offended by me." He was speaking directly to John's situation, to the one who had done everything right and was now in a place that didn't look like a reward. Blessed is the one who is not offended when my timing doesn't match what you were expecting. And then after John's disciples had left, Jesus turned to the crowd and said something remarkable. He said, "Among those born of women, there has arisen no one greater than John the Baptist. The greatest person born of a woman was at the moment Jesus said those words sitting in a prison cell. Confused, waiting, not rescued by every visible measure. His story was ending in the wrong place at the wrong time. But Jesus was not measuring by visible measures. Here is what you need to understand about John's timeline. He was not behind. He was not forgotten. He was not abandoned. He was fulfilling his assignment with the exact faithfulness that Jesus publicly honored while being in circumstances that looked like failure from every external angle. The prison was not a malfunction in his calling. The prison was the final chapter of it and John could not see that from inside the cell. Neither can you see what your current chapter is building toward. I want to name something specifically now because I think it is the mechanism behind almost all of the I am behind feeling. The comparison trap in scripture is not a new problem. It is as old as the first two brothers. Cain and Abel brought offerings. God looked with favor on Abel's offering and not on Cain's. And instead of asking what he needed to change, instead of looking inward, Cain looked sideways at his brother. And Genesis 4:5 says, "So Cain was very angry and his face fell." The first murder in human history was downstream from comparison from looking at someone else's season and allowing it to redefine his own. Peter made the same mistake in the final chapter of John. Jesus had just reinstated him, just given him his commission. Feed my lambs, tend my sheep, feed my sheep. And then Jesus began to speak about how Peter would die. about the suffering that his calling would involve. And Peter's immediate response was to turn around and point at John and ask, "Lord, what about this man?" He had just been given a profound and personal commission. A conversation with the risen Christ about his specific calling and his specific future. And his first instinct was to compare, to ask why John's path looked different from his. Jesus's response to Peter is one of the most clarifying things he ever said. If it is my will that he remain until I come, what is that to you? You follow me. You follow me. Not him, not his timeline, not his path, not his pace. Your assignment is not his assignment. Your timeline is not his timeline. Your path is not his path. And the energy you spend comparing your chapter to someone else's chapter is energy that was meant to be given to the chapter you are actually in. There is a third reason God's timeline is invisible to you and it is the most important one. The most significant work God does in a person's life is almost always done in the hidden place before the visible thing under the surface. in the seasons that look from the outside like nothing is happening. Psalm 139-15 6 describes it with a precision that still astonishes me. My frame was not hidden from you when I was made in the secret place. When I was woven together in the depths of the earth, your eyes saw my unformed body. All the days ordained for me were written in your book before one of them came to be. Before you took a single breath, the days were written, not the years of visible achievement. The days, including the ones that feel like waiting, including the ones that feel like delay, including the ones that feel like everyone else is moving and you are standing still. Those days were written. They were not missed. They were not placeholders. They are part of the complete work. Joseph spent 13 years from age 17 to age 30 in conditions that would have destroyed most people. The pit, the house of Potifer, the prison. Not one of those years looked like progress toward the palace. Not one of them would have appeared from the outside as evidence of a man on his way to becoming second in command of Egypt. But something was happening under the surface in every one of those years. The Joseph who emerged from the prison at age 30 was not the same Joseph who fell into the pit at 17. The teenage boy who told his brothers about his dreams without apparently considering how they would receive it. That boy could not have been trusted with Egypt. The man who came out of 13 years of suffering, faithfulness, and waiting that man could be. The years that looked like delay were the years in which the man was being built who could carry what was coming. God was not late. God was constructing. And here is the question that changes everything about how you experience your current season. What is being built in you right now in this season that feels like waiting that could not be built any other way? Because if something is being built, if the hidden work is happening, even when you cannot see it, then you are not behind. You are in process. I need to be honest with you before I close because this message can be misused. You are not behind is not permission to be passive. It is not a justification for avoiding the hard thing, for staying in the comfortable thing, for refusing to take the next step God has made clear. Abraham believed God and it was credited to him as righteousness. But he also got up and went. He left. He left Haran. He packed everything and walked into a land he had not seen. The faith was active. The trust produced movement. So this is not a word that says sit down. Do nothing. God will bring it to you without your participation. This is a word that says stop measuring your movement against a timeline that was never yours. Keep moving. Keep faithful. Keep planting in the season you're in, but stop letting comparison to someone else's chapter tell you that your chapter is wrong. You are not behind, but you are responsible for the chapter you are in. Those two things are both true at the same time. So, let me bring this together practically. If the comparison has become a voice that narrates your life, that tells you what you should have by now, what you should have accomplished, where you should be, I want you to identify whose timeline that voice is using, because it is not using God's. God never gave you that schedule. Someone or something else did. If the waiting has made you believe the promise was wrong, that you misheard, that God forgot, that the thing you sensed coming was your imagination, I want you to sit with Abraham's 25 years, not because your timeline will be the same. It won't be, but because the pattern is the same. The promise came before the fulfillment. The circumstances contradicted the promise before they confirmed it. And the delay was not a mistake. It was the mechanism. And if you are in a season that looks from the outside like failure, like a prison, like a wilderness, like everyone else is moving and you are standing still. I want you to remember what Jesus said about John the Baptist while John was sitting in that cell. The greatest person born of a woman said about a man in prison who was confused who sent a question instead of a testimony who died without seeing the full fruit of what his faithfulness produced. Jesus was not measuring by the prison. He was measuring by the faithfulness. The morning Isaac was born. Abraham was 100 years old. He had spent 25 years with the promise and without the fulfillment. 25 years of the gap, of watching, of waiting, of the months that passed and the years that accumulated, and the body that aged past the point where any of this should have been possible, and then the child arrived. And scripture says, Abraham named him Isaac, which means laughter, because Sarah had laughed when she heard the promise, laughed at its impossibility, at the audacity of the timeline. And now the laughter was still there, but it had changed. It was no longer the laughter of disbelief. It was the laughter of someone who had waited long enough to see the impossible become real. The 25 years did not disappear. They did not become irrelevant. They became the foundation on which the miracle stood. Because without the 25 years, there was no miracle. There was only biology. The timeline was not the obstacle to the promise. The timeline was the container that made the promise what it needed to be. You are not behind. You are not forgotten. You are not on the wrong page of a story whose author has been paying attention to every chapter, including this one. The timeline you cannot see is being held by someone who can. fullTextVi: Bạn đang so sánh chương 3 của bạn với chương 20 của người khác. Và sự so sánh đang khiến bạn tin vào điều gì đó không đúng. Nó khiến bạn tin rằng mình đang ở phía sau, phía sau nơi mà lẽ ra bạn phải ở, phía sau đồng nghiệp của bạn, đằng sau một lịch trình vô hình nào đó mà mọi người xung quanh bạn dường như đang tuân theo ngoại trừ bạn. Đằng sau phiên bản cuộc sống mà bạn nghĩ bây giờ bạn đã có. Và đây là những gì niềm tin đó làm được. Nó biến mọi giai đoạn trong cuộc đời bạn thành bằng chứng của sự thất bại. Sự chờ đợi trở thành bằng chứng bạn đã làm sai điều gì đó. Sự chậm trễ trở thành sự xác nhận rằng Chúa đã quên bạn. Mùa bạn đang ở, bất kể là mùa nào, đều trở thành thứ để trốn thoát hơn là thứ gì đó để sinh sống. Nhưng tôi muốn cho bạn thấy một điều trong Kinh thánh sẽ thay đổi vĩnh viễn cách bạn đo thời gian. Trong kinh thánh, Chúa không hoạt động theo một dòng thời gian hữu hình. Anh ấy không đo lường sự tiến bộ theo cách bạn đo lường nó. Anh ấy không xác định thời gian theo cách bạn xác định. Và mọi người mà anh ấy từng sử dụng đều dựa trên mọi thước đo thời gian của con người. Muộn, sai tuổi, sai mùa, sai thời điểm và chính xác là nơi Chúa cần họ đến be. Nếu bạn đang đo lường cuộc đời mình bằng chiếc đồng hồ mà Chúa chưa bao giờ ban tặng bạn, cái này dành cho bạn. Trước khi chúng ta xem qua các ví dụ, tôi cần đặt tên cho thứ thực sự là xảy ra bên dưới bề mặt của sự so sánh. Khi bạn cảm thấy bị tụt lại phía sau, bạn không chỉ đang cảm thấy thiếu kiên nhẫn. Bạn đang đưa ra một tuyên bố thần học. Bạn đang ngầm nói rằng, tôi biết dòng thời gian của Chúa dành cho cuộc đời tôi là gì trông như thế nào, và đây không phải là nó. Đó là một giả định quan trọng bởi vì không nơi nào trong kinh thánh Chúa trao cho ai một lịch trình. Không nơi nào anh ấy nói ở tuổi 30 bạn nên có cái này, ở tuổi 35 lẽ ra bạn phải làm được điều đó Dòng thời gian mà bạn đang đo lường bản thân được tập hợp từ một nơi khác từ nền văn hóa so sánh với những gì đã có hiệu quả đối với một người có nhiệm vụ hoàn toàn khác với nhiệm vụ của bạn. Truyền-đạo 3:11 nói, "Đức Chúa Trời đã làm nên mọi sự tốt đẹp vào đúng thời điểm của nó. " Và sau đó nó nói điều gì đó hiếm khi được trích dẫn cùng với câu đó. Ngài cũng đã đặt sự vĩnh cửu trong lòng con người. Tuy nhiên, không ai có thể hiểu được những gì Đức Chúa Trời đã làm từ đầu đến cuối. Hãy đọc kỹ điều đó. Đức Chúa Trời đặt cho cõi vĩnh hằng chiếc hòm trọn vẹn theo mục đích của Ngài trong lòng bạn. Nhưng anh ấy đã làm nó nên bạn không thể nhìn thấy nó một cách trọn vẹn. Bạn có cảm giác rằng có điều gì đó quan trọng ở phía trước. Nhưng bạn không thể nhìn thấy dòng thời gian đầy đủ từ nơi bạn đang đứng. Và đó không phải là một lỗ hổng thiết kế. Đó là cố ý. Bởi vì nếu bạn có thể xem được toàn bộ dòng thời gian thì bạn sẽ không cần phải tin tưởng người nắm giữ nó. Cảm giác bị tụt lại phía sau hầu như luôn là triệu chứng của việc cố gắng nhìn nhiều dòng thời gian hơn những gì Chúa đã cho bạn quyền truy cập. Ví dụ rõ ràng nhất trong toàn bộ kinh thánh là Áp-ra-ham. Và tôi muốn xem xét nó một cách chậm rãi vì các chi tiết rất quan trọng. Áp-ra-ham được 75 tuổi khi Đức Chúa Trời thực hiện lời hứa lần đầu tiên. 75. Ông không có con. Sarah cằn cỗi. Và Chúa bảo ông rằng ông sẽ trở thành cha của nhiều dân tộc, rằng con cháu của ông sẽ đông như sao trên trời và cát trên bờ biển. Theo bất kỳ dòng thời gian nào của con người, thời điểm cho lời hứa này đã trôi qua. Người đàn ông 75 tuổi có vợ hiếm muộn không phải là điểm khởi đầu đầy hứa hẹn cho một quốc gia vĩ đại. Bất kỳ người quan sát hợp lý nào cũng sẽ nói: "Bạn đã quá muộn. Cửa sổ đã đóng lại. Điều này sẽ không xảy ra. " Nhưng Chúa không làm việc theo dòng thời gian của con người. Áp-ra-ham được 85 tuổi khi Đức Chúa Trời tái khẳng định giao ước. Vẫn không có con. Ông được 99 tuổi khi Chúa hiện ra với ông lần nữa, đổi tên từ Áp-ra-ham đến Áp-ra-ham, cha của nhiều dân tộc, và nói với ông rằng trong vòng một năm Sarah sẽ sinh con. Sarah đã 90 tuổi. Cô bật cười khi nghe điều đó. Sáng thế ký 18:12 ghi lại những gì cô ấy nghĩ bên trong lều. Sau khi tôi kiệt sức và chúa tôi già, liệu bây giờ tôi có niềm vui này? Cô ấy không hề hoài nghi. Cô ấy đang thực tế. Toán học đã không hoạt động. Sinh học đã không hoạt động. Không có gì về thời gian làm việc. Và Isaac được sinh ra vào năm sau. Áp-ra-ham đã 100 tuổi. 25 năm giữa lời hứa và sự thực hiện. 25 năm chứng kiến ​​gia đình người khác phát triển trong khi gia đình mình vẫn trống rỗng. 25 năm khoảng cách giữa điều Chúa phán và điều Áp-ra-ham có thể see. Và lưu ý rằng Chúa đã không xin lỗi về dòng thời gian. Ông không giải thích sự chậm trễ. Anh chỉ hỏi khi nghe thấy tiếng cười của Sarah. Có điều gì quá khó đối với Chúa không? Đây là kết quả mà cân nặng 25 năm đó tạo ra mà cân nặng 5 năm không thể có được. Vào thời điểm Y-sác được sinh ra, Áp-ra-ham và Sa-ra về mặt sinh học là không thể đã tự mình sản xuất ra anh ta. Không có lời giải thích nào của con người cho đứa trẻ. Lời giải thích duy nhất là Chúa. Và đó chính là vấn đề. Sự chậm trễ không phải là một trục trặc trong dòng thời gian. Sự chậm trễ là cơ chế mà phép lạ sẽ trở nên rõ ràng. Nếu đứa trẻ được sinh ra sớm hơn thì cơ chế sinh học của con người có thể đã giành được công lao đó. Ở mức 190, không có lời giải thích nào khác. Điều bạn đang chờ đợi có thể được tính thời gian chính xác để khi nó đến lúc chỉ có một lời giải thích khả dĩ cho nó. Hãy để tôi hỏi bạn một câu trước khi chúng ta tiếp tục và tôi muốn bạn ngồi với nó một cách trung thực. Khi bạn nói rằng bạn cảm thấy đằng sau chính xác là gì? Đứng sau ai? Dòng thời gian đó đến từ đâu? Ai đưa nó cho bạn và nói với bạn rằng nó là của Chúa? Bởi vì đây là điều thường xuyên xảy ra. Ai đó xung quanh bạn kết hôn, được thăng chức, ra mắt một điều gì đó quan trọng, có một đứa con và mà không nhận ra điều đó, dòng thời gian của họ sẽ trở thành khuôn mẫu cho dòng thời gian của bạn. Chương 20 của họ trở thành chương 3 của bạn và bạn dành sức lực để đau buồn lịch trình mà ngay từ đầu chưa bao giờ là của bạn. Sự so sánh không chỉ gây tổn hại về mặt cảm xúc mà còn gây nhầm lẫn về mặt thần học. Nó giả định rằng Chúa đang truyền tải cùng một câu chuyện cho mọi người tại cùng một nhịp độ. Và Kinh Thánh không ủng hộ giả định đó, không chỉ một lần. Ví dụ thứ hai tôi muốn đưa bạn đến là một trong những những câu chuyện tàn khốc lặng lẽ trong Tin Mừng.
